guide.summary: Creating the Google OAuth client takes under an hour. The scopes you need decide how hard the rest is. Internal Workspace tools and testing builds (up to 100 users) need no review. A public app that uses only gmail.send (sensitive) needs brand and sensitive-scope verification, typically a few business days. An agent that reads inboxes needs restricted scopes (readonly/modify/compose). For those, Google requires restricted-scope verification plus an annual third-party security assessment (CASA) when data passes through a server. Plan for weeks, not days.

composio.note: Composio's managed Gmail app works for prototypes. On it, users see 'Composio' on the consent screen, Google quota is shared with other Composio users, and trigger polling has a 15-minute minimum. Adding scopes beyond Composio's defaults causes 'App is blocked'. For production you bring your own Google OAuth client. Register the redirect URI shown in your Composio dashboard; don't copy one from docs, because Composio's pages show two different ones.

need_own_app.answer: Not to prototype: Composio's managed Gmail app works today. To launch, almost always: for your own name on the consent screen, your own quota, and permissions beyond Composio's defaults.
reasons: Consent screen should show your app, not 'Composio wants to access your account' (c41)
Composio's managed app shares Google quota across all Composio users (c40)
You need scopes beyond Composio's defaults, e.g. gmail.settings.basic for filters; otherwise users hit 'App is blocked' (c39)
Triggers: managed auth polls no faster than every 15 minutes (c45)
Enterprise customers whose Workspace admins allowlist apps by client ID will want to trust your client, not a shared one (c61)

scenarios.label: Prototype or personal use
scenarios.when_this_applies: You are building or demoing, and you or a known group of up to 100 people connect Gmail. Either use Composio's managed app or your own External client left in Testing status.

hands_on.estimate: 0 min (managed app) / 30-60 min (own client in Testing)
hands_on.basis: Estimate from step count (project, Gmail API, consent setup, client, Composio auth config), not measured

waiting.basis: Development/testing and personal use are exempt from verification (c19, c20)

scenarios.approval: None. Test users see a warning screen, and grants plus refresh tokens expire after 7 days in Testing (c11, c35, c58). The test-user limit is 100 (c10).

scenarios.label: Internal tool, your company only
scenarios.when_this_applies: Only people in your own Workspace / Cloud Identity organization connect, and the Cloud project is owned by that organization. Any Gmail scope, including restricted ones.

hands_on.basis: Estimate from step count, not measured; no verification materials needed (c18)

waiting.estimate: None from Google; possibly your Workspace admin
waiting.basis: Internal apps need no Google review even for restricted scopes (c18), but admins may need to trust the app for high-risk Gmail scopes (c16, c61)

scenarios.approval: No Google verification. Your Workspace admin may need to mark the app Trusted for high-risk Gmail scopes.
extras: Your Workspace admin may need to trust it

scenarios.label: Public app that only sends email
scenarios.when_this_applies: A public product where any Google user connects, and the agent only sends email (no reading, drafting or labeling beyond non-sensitive scopes).

hands_on.basis: Estimate, not measured: homepage + privacy policy, domain verification, scope justification, demo video, submission (c21, c24-c27)

waiting.estimate: About 3-5 business days typical; brand check minutes to 2-3 business days
waiting.basis: Google's stated typical times (c8, c9); Google also warns verification can take several months (c51)

scenarios.approval: Brand verification + sensitive-scope verification. No security assessment (gmail.send is sensitive, not restricted: c1).

scenarios.label: Public agent that reads inboxes
scenarios.when_this_applies: A public product whose agent reads, triages, drafts or modifies mail (gmail.readonly / modify / compose / metadata), with tokens and data handled on servers (yours or Composio's).

hands_on.basis: Everything in s3 plus CASA security assessment prep and remediation; Nango reports 10-20 days for teams with no prior security audit (c65). Not measured.

waiting.estimate: Several weeks (Google); 5-20 days reported when well prepared
waiting.basis: Google: 'several weeks' (c7), possibly months (c51). Vendor report: 5-20 days (c65). No official CASA duration (c70).

scenarios.approval: Brand verification, restricted-scope verification, and a CASA security assessment by a Google-approved assessor (c5, c6).
scenarios.shortcut: Only need to send email? Ask for gmail.send alone. It needs no security assessment (c1).

prerequisites.title: Google account with Cloud Console access
prerequisites.detail: To create projects and OAuth clients. For s2 the project must sit in your Workspace organization.

prerequisites.title: Separate Cloud projects for dev and production
prerequisites.detail: Google requires one project per deployment tier. Your dev project keeps its own 100-test-user budget.

prerequisites.title: Composio project and API key
prerequisites.detail: To create a Gmail auth config with your own credentials and read the redirect URI from the dashboard.

prerequisites.title: A domain you control
prerequisites.detail: Homepage and privacy policy hosted on it, and ownership verified in Google Search Console by a project owner/editor.

prerequisites.title: Final list of Gmail scopes
prerequisites.detail: Map every agent tool you will expose to the narrowest scope. Whether you need send-only or read access decides between s3 and s4.

prerequisites.title: Security posture for restricted scopes
prerequisites.detail: Tokens encrypted at rest, prompt-injection protection, and readiness for a CASA assessment.

steps.title: Pick the scenario and the narrowest scopes
steps.detail: List the Composio Gmail tools your agent will call and map each to a Gmail scope. Prefer gmail.send (sensitive) or gmail.labels (non-sensitive). Note that gmail.compose and gmail.modify are restricted. Don't mix gmail.metadata with content scopes.
steps.done_when: Written scope list with a one-line reason per scope

steps.title: Create Cloud projects (dev and prod)
steps.detail: In Google Cloud Console create a project per tier. For an internal tool, create it inside your Workspace organization.
steps.done_when: Project IDs exist for dev and prod

steps.title: Enable the Gmail API
steps.detail: APIs & Services > Library > Gmail API > Enable, in every project whose client you use. An agent with an authenticated gcloud session can run `gcloud services enable gmail.googleapis.com`.
steps.done_when: Gmail API shows as Enabled

steps.title: Configure Google Auth Platform: Branding and Audience
steps.detail: Google Auth Platform > Get started: app name (don't use names like 'Gmail for Android'), user support email, Audience = Internal (s2) or External (s1, s3, s4), developer contact email. For External, add test users under Audience.
steps.done_when: Branding and Audience pages saved; test users listed

steps.title: Start a Composio auth config and copy its redirect URI
steps.detail: Composio dashboard > Create Auth Config > Gmail > OAuth2 > use your own developer credentials. Copy the redirect URI the dashboard shows. If you will go through verification (s3, s4), plan to proxy it through your own domain instead (see Traps).
steps.done_when: You have the exact redirect URI string from your dashboard

steps.title: Create the OAuth client
steps.detail: Google Auth Platform > Clients > Create client > Web application. Add the redirect URI from the previous step exactly. Copy the client ID and secret.
steps.done_when: Client ID and secret in hand

steps.title: Declare scopes on Data Access
steps.detail: Add exactly the scopes from step 1. These must match what Composio requests, or users get the unverified-app screen.
steps.done_when: Data Access lists the same scopes as your Composio auth config

steps.title: Finish the Composio auth config and wire it into sessions
steps.detail: Paste client ID/secret and the same scopes into the auth config, save, then pass the ac_ ID in authConfigs (keyed by toolkit) when creating sessions. An agent can write this code. Pasting secrets into the dashboard is yours.
steps.done_when: A session created in code uses your auth config

steps.title: Connect a test account end to end
steps.detail: Connect a test user, confirm the consent screen shows your app/domain, and run one send and one read tool. In Testing, expect the warning screen and a 7-day grant.
steps.done_when: Tool calls succeed with your connected account

steps.title: Ask your Workspace admin to trust the app (if needed)
steps.detail: If users get admin_policy_enforced, the admin must mark your client ID Trusted in Admin console > Security > API controls.
steps.done_when: Users in the org can grant Gmail scopes

steps.title: Publish homepage and privacy policy
steps.detail: Draft a homepage that describes the app (not just a login page) and a privacy policy covering how Gmail data is accessed, used, stored and shared, plus Limited Use and the AI-training restriction. You review and publish them on your domain.
steps.done_when: Both pages public on your domain and linked from Branding

steps.title: Verify domains and fix the redirect domain
steps.detail: Verify your domain in Google Search Console with a project owner/editor account, and add it to Authorized domains. Authorized domains must cover your redirect URI. If the redirect is on Composio's domain, switch to a proxy endpoint on your domain that 302s to Composio. An agent can write the proxy; update the URI in both Google and Composio.
steps.done_when: All authorized domains show verified

steps.title: Run and publish brand verification
steps.detail: Branding > Verify Branding (automated, usually minutes; manual fallback 2-3 business days). Publish branding within 7 days of a pass.
steps.done_when: Branding status is Published

steps.title: Write scope justifications
steps.detail: For each sensitive/restricted scope: the feature, why a narrower scope fails, and where it appears in the UI. For s4, pick the Gmail approved use case (e.g. productivity / AI summaries).
steps.done_when: Justification text ready to paste

steps.title: Record the demo video
steps.detail: An agent can draft the script. You record the English OAuth flow, consent screen with app name, client ID in the address bar, and each scope's feature in use. Agent platforms must show how workflows are created and which way data flows. Upload to YouTube as Unlisted.
steps.done_when: Unlisted YouTube link

steps.title: Submit data-access verification
steps.detail: Verification Center: declare scopes, add justification and video, submit. Reply quickly to Trust & Safety emails sent to your developer contact.
steps.done_when: Submission acknowledged

steps.title: Wait for Google review
steps.detail: Sensitive: typically 3-5 business days. Restricted: several weeks. Either can take longer.
steps.done_when: Data access status approved

steps.title: Complete the CASA security assessment
steps.detail: Pick a Google-empanelled assessor, scan and remediate. Encrypt tokens at rest and add prompt-injection protection. The assessor sends the letter to Google. An agent can run scans and help fix findings.
steps.done_when: Assessor's Letter of Assessment accepted by Google

steps.title: Publish the app to production
steps.detail: Audience > Publish app. Make sure code requests only the approved scopes.
steps.done_when: Publishing status In production, no unverified-app screen

steps.title: Calendar the annual re-assessment
steps.detail: Re-verify and re-assess at least every 12 months from the LOA date. Keep owner/editor and contact emails current so the notice reaches you.
steps.done_when: Reminder set before the 12-month mark

traps.title: Redirect on Composio's domain blocks verification
traps.detail: Authorized domains must include your redirect URI's domain, and you must prove ownership in Search Console. You can't do that for Composio's domain, so proxy the callback through your own domain before submitting. (This is an inference from c22 + c23; not stated by either party.)

traps.title: gmail.compose and gmail.modify are restricted, not sensitive
traps.detail: Drafting replies or labeling read mail puts you on the restricted track with CASA. Only gmail.send (and add-on scopes) are sensitive.

traps.title: AI-agent-specific policy rules
traps.detail: Workspace policy requires prompt-injection protection and bans training general models on user Gmail data. Reviewers of task-automation apps expect the video to show data flow.

traps.title: Testing mode breaks agents weekly
traps.detail: External apps in Testing get grants and refresh tokens that expire after 7 days, so background agents lose access silently. The only exception is name/email/profile scopes, which Gmail never fits.

traps.title: The 100-user caps are lifetime
traps.detail: Unverified production apps get 100 new users ever, with no reset. Test-user slots are consumed as soon as a user is added. Use a separate dev project.

traps.title: Scope drift between Google and Composio
traps.detail: If the auth config requests a scope not declared/approved on Data Access, users get the unverified screen or 'App is blocked'.

traps.title: Refresh-token limits
traps.detail: Google: 100 per account per client ID, oldest silently revoked. Composio's FAQ says ~50. Re-connecting the same user repeatedly in tests can revoke live tokens.

traps.title: New quota model for new projects
traps.detail: Projects created on or after 1 May 2026 get new Gmail quotas (6,000 units/min/user) and a daily billing threshold. Google has not published pricing above it yet.

traps.title: Name rules and idle clients
traps.detail: Don't put 'Gmail' or 'Google' in the app name. OAuth clients unused for 6 months can be deleted.

blockers.what_it_means: An Internal app is being authorized by a user outside your organization.
blockers.what_to_do: Use an account in the org, or switch Audience to External (which brings verification).

blockers.what_it_means: Sensitive/restricted scopes not yet verified, or code requests scopes not declared. The 100-new-user cap is running.
blockers.what_to_do: Match code scopes to Data Access and submit for verification.
blockers.agent_can_help: Check scope parity and prepare the verification package.

blockers.what_it_means: Testing-mode 7-day token expiry, or the refresh-token limit revoked older tokens.
blockers.what_to_do: Reconnect; to stop it, publish and verify the app.
blockers.agent_can_help: Detect the pattern in logs and trigger re-auth prompts.

blockers.symptom: 'App is blocked' / 'This app is blocked' when connecting Gmail
blockers.what_it_means: The client requests scopes Google has not verified for it (often extra scopes added to Composio's managed app).
blockers.what_to_do: Remove the extra scopes, or use your own OAuth client and get those scopes verified.
blockers.agent_can_help: Diff the auth config's scopes against the Data Access list and approved scopes.

blockers.what_it_means: The user's Workspace admin restricts high-risk Gmail scopes to trusted apps.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask the admin to mark your client ID Trusted.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the admin request with client ID and scope list.

blockers.symptom: 'Gmail API has not been used in project ...'
blockers.what_it_means: The Gmail API is not enabled in the project that owns the client.
blockers.what_to_do: Enable it, wait a few minutes, retry.
blockers.agent_can_help: Run gcloud services enable if gcloud is authenticated.

blockers.symptom: invalid_client 'The OAuth client was not found.'
blockers.what_it_means: Wrong or deleted client ID in the auth config.
blockers.what_to_do: Re-copy the client ID from the Clients page into Composio.
blockers.agent_can_help: Validate the client ID against the authorize endpoint.

blockers.what_it_means: Shared quota on Composio's managed app, or per-user per-minute limits.
blockers.what_to_do: Use your own client for dedicated quota and add exponential backoff.
blockers.agent_can_help: Add backoff/retry to the agent's tool calls.

blockers.symptom: Under review for weeks with no reply
blockers.what_it_means: Developers report reviews sitting for 8+ weeks with no email from Google's Trust & Safety team (c71).
blockers.what_to_do: Reply on your existing verification case or use Google's OAuth verification support form. Drop every scope you don't call: one team was approved two days after removing unneeded scopes (c72).
blockers.agent_can_help: List the scopes your code actually calls and draft the reply.

blockers.symptom: The security assessment (CASA) email never arrived
blockers.what_it_means: Google's verification team sends the invitation. Developers report it going missing, even after checking spam (c73).
blockers.what_to_do: Check the project owner and support contact mailboxes, then reply on the verification case or use the OAuth verification support form. Only Google can resend it.

open_questions: Does using your own restricted-scope client through Composio count as server-side access requiring CASA? Assume yes; confirm with Google Trust & Safety during review (c68).
Which exact scopes does Composio's Gmail auth config request by default? Check the scope list in the Composio auth config UI (c69).
No official CASA cost or duration exists. Ask assessors for quotes; vendor reports put Tier 2 at ~$540-$720/yr (c66, c70).
Refresh-token limit: Google documents 100 per account per client ID, but Composio's FAQ says ~50. Confirm which applies to Composio-held tokens.
What will Google charge above the Gmail daily billing threshold? Google says details come later in 2026 (c48).

claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Task automation platforms must show in the demo video how API workflows are created and which way user data flows.
claims.quote: If your app is a task automation platform, your demonstration video must showcase how multiple API workflows are created and automated
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Test users see a warning screen before authorizing an app in Testing.
claims.quote: Google will display a warning message before allowing a specified test user to authorize scopes requested by your project's OAuth clients.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: A test user uses up a slot in the project's test-user quota as soon as they are added.
claims.quote: A test user consumes a project's test user quota once added to the project.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Without brand verification, the consent screen shows only your app's domain, not its name or logo.
claims.quote: Without verification, only your application domain will be visible to users.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Workspace admins can restrict Gmail's high-risk scopes (including gmail.send) to trusted apps.
claims.quote: Gmail, Google Drive, Docs, and Chat can also restrict access to a predefined list of high-risk OAuth scopes.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Composio's Google guide says default scopes are usually sufficient and that the redirect URI in Composio must match the one configured in GCP.
claims.quote: Redirect URI → must match the one you configured in GCP
claims.label: composio_docs

claims.text: Google's authorize endpoint rejects an unknown client_id by redirecting to an error page with invalid_client ('The OAuth client was not found.'), so a typo in the client ID fails before consent.
claims.label: probed

claims.text: The Google Auth Platform Branding page redirects to a Google sign-in; console setup needs a logged-in human (or an authenticated gcloud session).
claims.label: probed

claims.text: Nango (an integration vendor) reports 5-20 days from requesting review to fully verified for app verification plus CASA when well prepared, and that CASA, not Google's review, is usually the longer leg.
claims.quote: If you prepare with this guide, you can expect 5-20 days from requesting review being fully verified.
claims.label: reported
claims.note: Vendor blog, not Google. Not an official timeline.

claims.text: Nango reports CASA Tier 2 assessor prices of about $540-$720 (TAC Security), ~$700 (Netsentries), $3,000+ (Prescient Security), as of August 2025.
claims.quote: Prices are as of August 2025, if you have updates, let us know.
claims.label: reported
claims.note: Vendor-reported prices; Google publishes no cost.

claims.text: Nango reports that test users are permanent: you cannot reset the counter or remove them.
claims.quote: Test users are permanent: You cannot reset the counter or remove test users.
claims.label: reported
claims.note: Consistent with Google's 'consumes quota once added' wording but not stated by Google this strongly.

claims.text: Whether connecting Gmail through Composio with your own restricted-scope OAuth client counts as 'access from or through a third-party server' (and so requires CASA) is not stated by Google or Composio. Tokens and API calls go through Composio's backend, so assume yes.
claims.label: unknown
claims.note: Inference from c4/c5. Confirm with Google Trust & Safety during review.

claims.text: The exact default scopes Composio requests for Gmail (managed app or a new custom auth config) are not listed on the pages fetched.
claims.label: unknown
claims.note: Check the scope list shown in the Composio auth config UI.

claims.text: Google publishes no official cost or fixed duration for the CASA security assessment.
claims.label: unknown
reported
claims.text: A developer reports a sensitive-scope-only verification stuck under review for over 8 weeks, with no email from Trust & Safety.
claims.quote: has been stuck in “under review” for over 8 weeks

claims.label: reported
claims.text: One team reports verification took almost a month; after removing unnecessary scopes it was verified within two days.
claims.quote: we received an email within two days confirming that our application was verified.

claims.label: reported
claims.text: A developer reports never receiving the CASA invitation from Trust & Safety. The advice given: use the OAuth verification support form or reply to the existing case.
claims.quote: use the OAuth verification support form or reply to the existing verification case

guide.verdict: Under an hour for an internal tool. Weeks of Google review, a security assessment and a yearly re-check if your agent reads inboxes.

meta.review_note: Researched ahead of time under the same evidence rules as the live agent. Quotes re-checked against their source pages on 20 Oct 2026. Not yet hands-on tested.
